name: Media server (Essential)
description: Jellyfin and Seerr, set up and signed in to each other by the dashboard, for a library you fill yourself. Requests are collected but nothing fetches them.

access.note: The dashboard finishes every application's first-run setup itself, before anyone else can reach it, and signs every one in with one login: admin and a password it keeps. Reveal it, or change it, on the stack's page.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.description: The address Jellyfin opens at. Seerr gets its own beside it: media.example.com gives media-requests.example.com.

inputs.name: login-password
inputs.label: Password for every app
inputs.description: Every app signs in as admin with one password. Leave it empty and the dashboard makes one; change it later on the stack's page.

inputs.name: request-approval
inputs.label: Requests
inputs.description: Who decides what is fetched. People you let in to Seerr can always ask.

choices.label: You approve each request
choices.description: Nothing is fetched until an administrator approves it

choices.label: Approve automatically
choices.description: A request from anyone you let in is fetched at once

services.name: jellyfin
services.purpose: Plays the library on every screen, behind the domain

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web interface and the apps

volumes.name: media
volumes.purpose: Downloads and the library, on one volume so a finished download is moved into the library rather than copied

services.name: seerr
services.purpose: Where people search for a title and ask for it; signs in with Jellyfin accounts

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The request desk, at its own address beside the domain

volumes.name: seerr-config
volumes.purpose: settings.json, the database of users and requests, and the logs

update.notes: Back up first: Jellyfin and the managers migrate their databases on start and cannot go back without a restore. The stack configures itself again after every deploy.
